facts.raw_span: underwent transthoracic echocardiography as part of a routine medical checkup
which revealed a left ventricular mass
A chest radiograph revealed no active lung lesions
Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass originating from the left ventricular lateral wall, measuring 1.34 × 1.9 cm
Contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography showed the mass attached to the interventricular septum with focal contrast enhancement

concepts.why: The patient has a mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass originating from the left ventricular lateral wall, which is consistent with a left ventricular myxoma.
The patient has a mass attached to the interventricular septum with focal contrast enhancement, which could be consistent with a left ventricular fibroelastoma.
The patient has a left ventricular mass, which could be a cardiac lipoma, although it is less likely given the description of the mass.
The patient has a mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass, which could be consistent with a papillary fibroelastoma, although it is less likely given the location of the mass.

rationales.F03: Left ventricular mass is a key feature of left ventricular myxoma and other cardiac tumors.
